evidence.verdict: REFUTED (kill condition triggered): the fork policy does not avoid the compaction break. fork == summarise_in_place in cache behaviour, identical medians, 18/21 paired deltas exactly 0, permutation p=1.0, max |delta| 64 = one 64-grid block. fork breaks on 21/21 events, not once per fork.
evidence.cheapest: at the event turn sliding_window (median 1728, total 20928) because its post-compaction prompt is 1.8k tokens vs 6.2k and break_cost is ~the whole rewritten prompt; over the full 44-turn session summarise_in_place is cheapest (256,883 uncached vs 293,901 for sliding, hit rate 0.730 vs 0.592) because sliding re-anchors its window near the front of the context every turn and loses the reuse that summarise keeps.
evidence.grid_law_violations: 372/372 warm-append rows deviate from cached==64*floor(prompt/64); residual histogram 896:103, 1792:71, 1728:62, 2624:52, 3520:31, 832:18, 2688:17, 3584:7, 6976:3. The 64-grid append baseline in the brief does not hold on this server; break_cost is therefore reported as uncached - (prompt mod 64) as specified, and the fork-vs-edit comparison is a paired comparison on the same turns so it is unaffected.

next_unit_hint: The measured break is not 'rewriting' but 'new bytes at message 1': fork, summarise_in_place and any reorganisation put a different message at the front of the context, and everything after position 1 is uncached (54 events, cached=0 on the first post-event turn in 11/54, ~29% of the prompt uncached at the median event). A pointer renderer cannot avoid this either: the fork point is at the front, so the suffix is re-prefilled regardless of how short the pointer token is. If the project wants a cache-safe reorganisation it must keep all rewritten bytes at the TAIL (append-only fold at the end), not try to make forking cheap. Also: the shared renderer now emits the fork head verbatim, so fork == summarise by construction - any future fork claim must be tested against a renderer that actually emits a pointer, and this batch's fork arm should not be cited as evidence about pointer rendering.
